Thanks Tyler —

Attached is a short checklist + a tiny sim we ran (PulsePath-MAP-unit-econ-v1.xlsx / token-econ-sims-brief.csv). High level summary below and proposed gating criteria for the MAP:

- Baseline tokens/$: we start with our hosted price profile for the selected model (open-model q4a) — currently $0.0018 per 1k generated tokens as a baseline for the SAT model variant. For MAP planning we use an "effective tokens/$" which factors batching/caching.
- Tokens per interaction: you mentioned avg 120 tokens per user flow in the call; we modeled 80–160 tokens to cover range.
- Caching assumptions: prefix caching (rolled KV cache) with an expected hit-rate range of 30%–60% depending on repeatability of prompts.
- Batching: default conservative batch window 25ms targeting 6–10 requests/batch for POC concurrency; we can tune to tighter latency SLOs.
- Fallbacks: we include automatic low-cost variant fallback for burst traffic that hits dedicated limits.

Proposed MAP gating for pre-POC signoff (suggested acceptance thresholds):
1) Effective tokens/$ <= 0.0008 for steady-state simulated traffic (this includes caching + batching uplift).
2) End-to-end 95th latency for the user flow <= 250ms in our staged region.
3) KV cache hit-rate >= 35% for the top-10 repeated prompts (if your UX uses templated prompts).

Next steps: I looped in Karthik for runtime numbers and Vivek for commercial/commit guidance. If those thresholds look reasonable, we’ll update the MAP spreadsheet and lock the DocuSign SOW stub + demo slot 07/07 10:00 PT.

Quick technical notes on the assumptions in Stephanie's sheet —

Tyler / team,

A few clarifications so the MAP numbers map to what our runtime will actually deliver:

- "Effective tokens/$" calc: we use published tokens-per-dollar then divide by (1 - cache_hit_rate) * batching_efficiency. For the POC spreadsheet we assumed batching_efficiency = 1.15 (i.e., 15% additional throughput due to batching) which is conservative for small batches. If you do larger batch windows we commonly see 25%–40% improvements on throughput.
- Cache hit-rate: KV prefix caching is great for templated prompts. Expect 20%–40% hit-rate out of the box; 40%+ if you pre-warm frequent prefixes or add a small UX-side session key. We modeled 35% as the MAP baseline.
- Batch sizing: the 25ms window targets latency-sensitive POC flows. That typically yields 4–12 requests per batch depending on arrival pattern. If your traffic is burstier during certain flows we can move to a 50ms window for higher batching and better tokens/$ at the cost of ~20–30ms median latency increase.
- Quantization/variant: we recommend testing the int8 variant in the eval phase — it reduces model compute cost by ~1.6x in our infra but increases the risk of small generation quality regressions; include a quality regression test in the MAP.

Practical recommendation: in the MAP acceptance criteria include a small matrix: simulated traffic (low/medium/high) x cache-policy (none/default/warm) x batch-window (25/50/100ms) — run through those 9 sims and accept if effective tokens/$ is within 10% of the baseline for medium. That gives a defensible procurement commit.

Happy to run the sims if you share a small sample of typical prompts and a concurrency profile.

— Karthik
